ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening at onboarding and at least annually thereafter of all directors, officers, UBOs, shareholders, authorized signatories, and material counterparties against: (i) FINTRAC PEP definitions under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act; (ii) United Nations Security Council sanctions lists and Canadian regulations under the United Nations Act; (iii) the Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List under the Special Economic Measures Act and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act; (iv) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists when US-dollar clearing and Mercury ACH are used; (v) EU and UK consolidated sanctions lists when Wise or wire payments are settled through European banks. Enhanced due diligence is triggered by PEP status, significant adverse media, sanctions flags, high-risk jurisdiction residency, or inconsistent commercial substance. Screening results and risk rationales must be documented and retained for at least five years in accordance with FINTRAC record-keeping rules.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The proposed corporate name must be in the Latin script and must contain a mandatory legal element: 'Limited', 'Limitée', 'Incorporated', 'Incorporée', 'Corporation', or an applicable abbreviation such as 'Ltd.', 'Ltee.', 'Inc.', or 'Corp.'. A NUANS-style Ontario Name Search Report is required before filing and cannot be older than 90 days at the time of filing. French-language accents and diacritical marks are permitted; non-Latin names must be romanized or transliterated into the Latin script. The corporate name must not be deceptively similar to an existing Ontario, federal, or other Canadian business name. English and French versions of a name may be filed, but each version must independently comply with Ontario naming policies and clearly identify the corporation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the Director of Corporate and Compliance Services rejects or conditions a proposed name, the applicant should first submit a Name Reservation/Renewal request through the Ontario Business Registry with a fresh Name Search Report and a concise written submission on distinctiveness, phonetic and visual similarity, and fair use of any sensitive token. Where a name is refused because of a prohibited or regulated token, the applicant may obtain prior written approval or consent from the relevant regulator, such as the Financial Services Regulatory Authority of Ontario for financial services tokens, and resubmit. A formal administrative review may be requested by letter to the Companies and Capital Marketplace Branch of the Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery; if the Director maintains the refusal, judicial review may be pursued under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. J.1, in the Ontario Superior Court of Justice. In parallel, a new name reservation with a fresh Name Search Report and a revised corporate name may be filed without delay. Name reservations may be renewed for successive 90-day periods on payment of the applicable renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable. The OBCA requires a registered office in Ontario that is a physical, serviceable address; a post office box alone is not acceptable. A commercial virtual-office arrangement with a street address, mail forwarding, and process-service acceptance is acceptable for an affiliated media-buying corporation. However, Canadian financial institutions and FINTRAC-regulated entities may treat a bare virtual office without any operational or management presence in Canada as an enhanced due diligence factor, and banks such as Mercury or Wise may request additional evidence of substance before opening accounts. Actual accounting records, director decision-making, and digital advertising operations may be located abroad, but the registered office, registered agent, and corporate books must remain legally available in Ontario.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low. The estimated annual probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection by ServiceOntario or by federal corporate authorities is 1-3% for a non-regulated digital-advertising corporation. The probability increases materially to approximately 15-25% if the Canada Revenue Agency commences an income tax or HST audit, if the corporation claims input tax credits disproportionate to its declared operations, or if FINTRAC determines that the affiliate-media-buying payment flows constitute a money-services-business activity requiring a registration.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. B.16, as amended (OBCA), ss. 5, 10, 116, 118, 140, 186; O. Reg. 14/01 (Forms 1 and 2)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery — Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (ServiceOntario)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (Form 1 under O. Reg. 14/01)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital and no escrow requirement under the OBCA. Consideration for shares is fixed by the directors (cash, property, or past services). At least one incorporator is required. If the board has fewer than four directors, at least one director must be a resident Canadian; for boards of four or more, at least 25% of directors must be resident Canadians.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION — RESOLVED, that the Articles of Incorporation submitted under the Ontario Business Corporations Act are ratified and adopted; that the issuance of 100 common shares at CAD $0.10 each to the subscribing incorporator is approved and allotted; that By-Law No. 1 governing the management of the Corporation is adopted; that the registered office is established at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation; that [Name A] be appointed President, [Name B] Secretary, and [Name C] Treasurer; and that the officers are authorized to open bank accounts, execute contracts, and complete all post-incorporation filings. The Corporation expressly acknowledges its obligations under the Income Tax Act (Canada) and Ontario's Corporations Information Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario and Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (NUANS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a Name Search Report request through a licensed Ontario search house or ServiceOntario online for the proposed corporate name (e.g., 'AFFILIATE MEDIA BUYING HOLDINGS INC.'). Confirm the name is distinguishable and not prohibited under O. Reg. 14/01, s. 3, and review the Canadian Trademarks Database for conflicts. Submit up to three alternate names and retain the Ontario Name Report file number to include in Form 1. The reservation is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name (with up to 3 alternates)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused for confusing similarity, file a new Name Search Report with alternate names. For minor conflicts, submit written consent from the owner of the confusing name or apply to the Minister under OBCA s. 9 for discretionary approval.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario e-filing portal / Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CPSPB)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete Form 1 (Articles of Incorporation), including the registered office address (a physical address in Ontario), share structure (e.g., Class A common voting shares and Class B non-voting shares as needed), restrictions on share transfers, and first directors. Execute the incorporator's attestation, upload the Name Search Report file number, pay the CAD $360 filing fee, and submit through ServiceOntario's online business incorporation service. Receive the Certificate of Incorporation and the Ontario Business Number connection notice.
required_dossiers: NUANS Name Search Report file number
Consent to Act as Director (Form 2) for each proposed director
Payment of CAD $360 (approx. USD $270) filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CPSPB rejects or queries the filing, cure within the notice period by filing Articles of Amendment under OBCA s. 186 for defective provisions or re-file Form 1 with corrected data. A rejected fee payment must be re-tendered with the applicable resubmission fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: CRA and Ontario Tax Account Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online (BRO); Ontario Ministry of Finance (EHT); WSIB
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon issuance of the 9-digit Business Number (BN), register via BRO for GST/HST (s. 240, Excise Tax Act) and payroll deductions (s. 82, Income Tax Act); the corporate income tax account is created automatically. Register for Ontario Employer Health Tax (EHT) when annual Ontario payroll reaches CAD $1,000,000 or proactively to obtain an EHT account; register with WSIB for workplace insurance when hiring. File the Ontario Corporations Information Act Initial Return within 60 days after incorporation.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the BN is not auto-issued within 5 business days, contact the CRA Business Window (1-800-959-5525). EHT registration disputes may be objected to under the Ontario EHT Act within 180 days of the notice of assessment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporation's registered office, corporate counsel, and transfer agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold or waive the first shareholders' meeting; adopt the First Board Resolution and By-Law No. 1; issue share certificates to the subscriber; establish the share register and director register (OBCA s. 140) at the registered office; and record the officer appointment and banking resolutions. Maintain the minute book in English with OBCA-compliant records.
required_dossiers: Waiver of notice (if no formal meeting) under OBCA s. 114(6)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If statutory records are incomplete, cure by executing a written waiver signed by all shareholders and directors and re-executing the relevant resolutions. Late Initial Return filings are accepted with explanatory correspondence to ServiceOntario.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Occupancy and Business Licensing Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal licensing office (e.g., City of Toronto Municipal Licensing & Standards) and local building department
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Verify whether the leased office's zoning classification permits administrative media buying; obtain a Certificate of Occupancy (Building Code, O. Reg. 332/12); schedule a Fire Code inspection (O. Reg. 213/07); apply for a municipal business licence only where the municipality requires one for the premises. Confirm that digital advertising arbitrage does not constitute a regulated provincial activity and retain an exemption memorandum in the corporate records.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Occupancy or zoning certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality issues an occupancy deficiency notice, remedy the physical items and appeal to the Ontario Building Code Commission (O. Reg. 332/12) or seek an order review from the Fire Marshal's office under O. Reg. 213/07.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541810 affiliate media buying is an office-based digital service with no industrial establishment. Ontario Ministry of Labour, Immigration, Training and Skills Development (MLITSD) retains general workplace jurisdiction.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None required — no provincial operational or manufacturing permit applies to digital performance media buying; only municipal occupancy and workplace compliance attach.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks (MECP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — Schedule 2/Table 1 industrial thresholds under O. Reg. 524/98 (Environmental Assessment Act) and O. Reg. 455/09 (EASR) are not triggered by administrative office use.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to affiliate media buying operations. Where electronic equipment wastes are generated, comply with O. Reg. 347/02 (waste management) and municipal sewer by-laws (Toronto Municipal Code, Chapter 681); voluntary GHG reporting under O. Reg. 390/18 applies only if the corporation's statutory emission threshold is crossed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Compliance required with: Ontario Fire Code, O. Reg. 213/07 (fire safety plan, annual inspections, alarm testing); Building Code Act, 1992, O. Reg. 332/12 (occupancy certificate); Occupational Health and Safety Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. O.1 (harassment and violence policies, first aid kits under R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 1101); Workplace Safety and Insurance Act, 1997, S.O. 1997, c. 16, Sch. A (WSIB coverage for officers and employees).

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal tax administration for corporate income tax, GST/HST, and payroll; Ontario corporate income tax is administered by the CRA on behalf of the Ontario Ministry of Finance under the Tax Collection Agreements Act (single unified T2 filing). Portals: CRA My Business Account (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-business.html), Business Registration Online (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-business/business-registration-online.html), GST/HST NETFILE, and the Ontario Business Registry (https://www.ontario.ca/page/business-registry).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate under the Canada Business Corporations Act (CBCA) via Corporations Canada or under the Ontario Business Corporations Act (OBCA) via the Ontario Business Registry, obtaining a federal incorporation number or Ontario Corporation Number. Step 2: Register with the CRA through Business Registration Online or Form RC1 to obtain the 9-digit Business Number (BN) with program accounts: Corporation Income Tax (RC0001), GST/HST (RT0001), Payroll (RP0001 if employees) and Import/Export (RM0001 if goods cross borders). Step 3: A non-resident-controlled corporation must file Form RC4150 (Non-Resident Corporation Information Return) and maintain a registered Canadian director or authorized representative for service of process. Step 4: Register for GST/HST when worldwide taxable supplies exceed C$30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the preceding four quarters; voluntary registration is strongly recommended for affiliate media buyers to claim input tax credits (ITCs) and to zero-rate export services. Step 5: Enroll in CRA electronic services (My Business Account, Represent a Client, GST/HST NETFILE, T2 Corporation Internet Filing) and set up electronic payments, which are mandatory for CRA remittances of C$10,000 or more.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. A Canadian business corporation is a separate taxpayer from its shareholders; there is no pass-through regime and no check-the-box election in Canada. A corporation resident in Canada is taxed on worldwide income (Income Tax Act, R.S.C. 1985, c.1 (5th Supp.), s.2(1)); a non-resident corporation is taxed on Canadian-source business income and taxable Canadian property dispositions (ITA s.2(3), s.115, s.253). Ontario levies provincial corporate income tax at 8% on the first C$500,000 of active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) and 11.5% on general corporate income. No tax-exempt zone or industry-specific exemption applies to digital advertising or affiliate media buying in Ontario.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists; classification follows incorporation law. Available elections include: (i) ITA s.85(1) rollover on property transfers into the corporation; (ii) ITA s.216 election for non-residents on net Canadian rental income; (iii) ITA s.217 election for non-residents on certain Canadian pension income; (iv) associated-corporation elections under ITA s.256 for allocating the C$500,000 small business deduction; and (v) CCPC elections on the T2 return for refundable dividend tax accounts. Hybrid-mismatch constraints directly relevant to foreign-owned media-buying corporations: ITA ss.18.2 and 18.4 deny deductions for hybrid mismatch arrangements; ITA s.18(4) thin-capitalization limits interest deductions on shareholder debt to a 1.5:1 debt-to-equity ratio; and Part II.2 foreign affiliate dumping tax (ITA s.212.3, Form RC4651) may apply to excessive capital injections from non-resident shareholders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as central bank; Canada has no dedicated foreign-exchange control administration. Cross-border monetary and AML reporting is administered by FINTRAC under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full convertibility of the Canadian dollar on both current-account and capital-account transactions. There are no general exchange controls, no requirement for central bank approval on dividend repatriation, and no restrictions on converting CAD into major currencies. However, any transfer of funds exceeding CAD 10,000 into or out of Canada is reportable to FINTRAC, and certain outbound payments to high-risk jurisdictions must satisfy enhanced due diligence standards. Profit remittance to foreign shareholders is freely permitted after compliance with corporate law solvency tests and tax withholding reporting (Part XIII T5 filings for dividends).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Canada imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no prescribed repatriation timeline for export receipts. Exporters may retain proceeds in any permitted currency. Nevertheless, all receipts crossing the border must be traceable through FINTRAC-reporting channels, and underlying commercial documents must be retained to substantiate the source and purpose of export earnings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)
Bank of Montreal (BMO Bank of Montreal)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-High for ancillary cross-border payment flows, but not recommended as the sole primary banking relationship. Legally, a foreign offshore digital EMI must be registered as a money-services business (MSB) in Canada if it conducts payment services for Canadian resident entities, or must obtain a limited-services arrangement through a chartered Canadian bank. Wise Canada holds an MSB licence in Canada and can provide multi-currency operating rails. Mercury is oriented principally to US entities and typically does not support a pure Ontario business corporation account; therefore it should be used only for distinctly separate US-based affiliated entities, not for routing the Canadian treasury. The Canadian operating entity must maintain a core account at a tier-1 Schedule I Canadian bank to ensure regulatory certainty, ISO 20022 wire routing, and same-day CAD clearing.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is permitted for a standard Ontario business corporation through video identity verification at most major Canadian Schedule I banks. Directors and authorized signatories do not generally need to appear physically at a branch for a basic operating account, provided they pass cryptographic identity verification, provide a notarized certificate of incumbency, and submit certified corporate registry documents. However, for capital escrow accounts, high-risk offshore ownership structures, or accounts receiving inbound shareholder loans, banks may require an in-person meeting or an enhanced due-diligence interview. The board should therefore budget one physical or video-intensive KYC interview for the ultimate beneficial owner and the Canadian director to prevent onboarding delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Company name or shareholder structure indicates a complex multi-tier foreign holding chain with nominee officers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Corporate registry extract from Corporations Canada / Ontario Ministry of Government and Consumer Services; organizational chart from ultimate beneficial owner to each intermediate entity; notarized declarations of beneficial ownership in the prescribed FINTRAC format; passport copies of all 25%-plus owners; board resolution authorizing account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Business description of 'media buying' or 'affiliate advertising' with high-volume outbound payments to numerous foreign publishers and traffic suppliers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed signed advertiser and media-buying agency agreements; ad platform or demand-side platform (DSP) statements; copy of publisher contracts and payment terms; sample campaign performance reports; invoices for media inventory; business plan showing traffic arbitrage model and expected payout cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection classified as a shareholder loan or intercompany advance shortly before high-frequency outbound transfers.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Unanimous shareholder agreement and loan agreement executed on arm's-length terms; source-of-funds documentation from the lender's bank; explanation of commercial purpose; tax opinion or accountant's letter confirming loan v. paid-up capital treatment; projected treasury cash-flow forecast.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment beneficiaries are located in jurisdictions considered sanctioned, high-risk, or known for advertising fraud.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed KYB file for each high-risk counterparty, including beneficial owner names, business registrations, and proof of operating status; contractual audit right clause; sanctions screening results; anti-fraud and compliance policy; log of vetting performed and the reason the relationship is legitimate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid movement of funds between an operational CAD account and a fintech/EMI multi-currency wallet.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Concise treasury policy approved by the board; reconciliation ledger linking each wallet transfer to a specific commercial invoice; copies of the EMI's MSB registration in Canada; final beneficiary underlying invoices; monthly AML compliance sign-off.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from a foreign parent or shareholder must be routed through SWIFT WT (wire transfer) using the Canadian beneficiary bank's BIC and the Ontario entity's account number. The remittance details must state either 'Shareholder Loan', 'Equity Injection / Paid-in Capital', or 'Intercompany Advance' as the payment purpose; no government-issued transaction code is required in Canada, but the bank may ask for supporting purpose codes in its internal forms. A copy of the loan agreement, corporate resolution, and ownership chart must be provided to the receiving bank to release funds to the capital escrow or operating account without AML holds. For amounts equal to or greater than CAD 10,000, the bank will file a Large Cash Transaction / Cross-Border Transfer Report with FINTRAC; the entity must ensure the remitting account is held in the name of the same corporate beneficial owner or identified arm's-length financier to avoid a suspicious transaction report.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements to international media vendors, affiliate networks, DSPs, and data providers should use SWIFT MT103 for same-day or value-dated cross-border settlement when the beneficiary is not enrolled in Canadian direct clearing. For repeat high-value media buys of over CAD 50,000, a commercial letter of credit (MT700) is advisable where the counterparty requires payment assurance before delivering ad inventory; standby LC (MT760) can also support ongoing media-rate cards. Domestic publisher payments can use EFT/ACH or wire transfer through the operating bank. Each disbursement must include the invoice number, contract reference, and clear description (e.g., 'digital media purchase' or 'performance advertising services') in the remittance field. The entity must maintain a KYB file on each beneficiary and obtain a declaration confirming that the beneficiary is not a shell or sanctions-linked entity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable foreign-exchange forwards entered into with a Canadian Schedule I bank or an SEC/CIRO-regulated dealer, limited to hedges of real invoiced exposure.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) permitted for currencies that are not freely deliverable in Canada, provided the underlying commercial contract is documented and the counterparty is a regulated financial institution.
Cross-currency swaps for long-term committed advertising contracts denominated in USD, subject to board approval and documented underlying cash-flow exposure.

FX options bought or sold under an ISDA Master Agreement with a Canadian bank, provided the strategy is designated as a hedge on the treasury risk committee's hedge register and not intended for speculative gain.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery (MPBSD) – Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (ServiceOntario)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the corporation's incorporation anniversary date (e.g., June 1 anniversary → due August 30).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty CAD 100 if filed more than 60 days after anniversary; CAD 250 if more than one year late; CAD 500 if more than two years late; administrative dissolution may be initiated for two consecutive missed annual returns or three non-consecutive misses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T2 Corporation Income Tax Return (Federal and Ontario corporate income tax)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after the fiscal year-end (for December 31 year-end, due June 30).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid tax plus 1% per complete month (maximum 12%); compound daily interest on unpaid balances; director liability in cases of default.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset test under the Ontario Business Corporations Act. Audit is mandatory for distributing (public) corporations; non-distributing private corporations may waive annual auditor appointment by unanimous shareholder resolution each fiscal year (OBCA s.151). A shareholder or group holding at least 5% of issued shares may require an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as issued by the IASB, or Canadian GAAP for private enterprises (ASPE) under the CPA Canada Handbook; public corporations must apply IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ontario provincial corporations have no separate annual UBO/ISC filing. If the entity is a CBCA federal corporation, maintain and update the Individual with Significant Control (ISC) register within 15 days of any change; annual corporate return does not list shareholding transfers, but ownership changes must be reflected in the Register of Members.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (resolutions of directors and shareholders)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No advertising-sector or media-buying tax holiday. Canadian-controlled private corporations benefit from the small business deduction on the first C$500,000 of active business income, producing a combined federal/Ontario rate of 12.2%. Federal SR&ED provides a 35% refundable credit for eligible CCPC expenditures. Non-capital losses carry back 3 years and forward 20 years.
